blocks.title: Consistency
blocks.body:
Under \(P\),
\[
Y=Y(A)
\]
almost surely.

blocks.title: Conditional exchangeability
blocks.body:
Under \(P\),
\[
(Y(0),Y(1))\perp A\mid X .
\]

blocks.title: Fixed overlap
blocks.body:
For each cell \(k\), let
\[
p_k:=P(X=k),
\]
and, when \(p_k>0\), let
\[
\pi_k:=P(A=1\mid X=k).
\]
For every \(k\) with \(p_k>0\),
\[
\epsilon\le \pi_k\le 1-\epsilon .
\]

blocks.title: Mean normalization
blocks.body:
The law \(P\) carries an arm-cell outcome distribution for every arm \(a\in\{0,1\}\) and \emph{every} cell \(k\), zero-mass cells included; let \(\mu_{ak}\) denote its mean.  Whenever the arm-cell probability \(P(A=a,X=k)\) is positive, \(\mu_{ak}\) is the observed conditional mean \(E_P[Y\mid A=a,X=k]\).  Only supported cells are constrained: for every \(a\in\{0,1\}\) and every \(k\) with \(p_k>0\),
\[
|\mu_{ak}|\le M/2 .
\]

blocks.title: Approximate homogeneity
blocks.body:
For \emph{every} cell \(k\), let
\[
\tau_k:=\mu_{1k}-\mu_{0k}
\]
and
\[
\delta_k:=\tau_k-\sum_j p_j\tau_j ,
\]
both well defined on zero-mass cells as well.
The cell-effect deviations satisfy
\[
\max_{k:p_k>0}|\delta_k|\le \sigma M .
\]

blocks.title: Second central moment
blocks.body:
For every \(a\in\{0,1\}\) and every \(k\) with \(p_k>0\),
\[
E_P\!\left[(Y-\mu_{ak})^2\mid A=a,X=k\right]\le M^2 .
\]

blocks.title: Real-outcome model class \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}\)
Unrestricted-radius class \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}^{\mathrm{unr}}\)
Sample experiment \(\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}\)
blocks.body:
Let
\[
O:=(X,A,Y)\in\mathcal O:=\{1,\ldots,d\}\times\{0,1\}\times\mathbb R,
\]
and let \(P_O\) denote the observed-data law of \(O\) under \(P\). The \(n\)-sample observed-data experiments generated by \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}\) are
\[
\mathcal E_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}
:=
\left\{
Q_P^{(n)}=P_O^{\otimes n}:P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}
\right\}.
\]

blocks.title: Average treatment effect \(\tau(P)\)
blocks.body:
For a real-outcome finite-cell law \(P\) indexed by \(k=1,\ldots,d\) and an overlap parameter \(\epsilon\) with \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), assume consistency, conditional exchangeability of \((Y(0),Y(1))\) and \(A\) given \(X\) for measurable potential-outcome events, overlap \(\epsilon\le \pi_k\le 1-\epsilon\) whenever \(p_k>0\), and first-moment integrability of each arm-cell outcome law for every \(a\in\{0,1\}\) and positive-mass cell. With \(p_k\) the cell mass and \(\mu_{ak}\) the arm-cell conditional outcome mean, define
\[
\tau(P)
:=
\sum_{k=1}^{d}p_k(\mu_{1k}-\mu_{0k}).
\]

blocks.title: Polynomial estimator \(T_n^{\mathrm{poly}}\)
blocks.body:
For observations \(O_i=(X_i,A_i,Y_i)\), with \(X_i\in\{1,\ldots,d\}\), \(A_i\in\{0,1\}\), and \(Y_i\in\mathbb R\), fix a polynomial handle \((N,\rho)\) with \(\rho>0\).  Let \(L:=\log(en)\),
\[
D_6:=8\log(27/4),
\qquad
\alpha_0:=\min\left\{1,\frac{1}{64\log 6},\frac{1}{512D_6}\right\},
\qquad
K_n:=\left\lfloor \alpha_0 L\right\rfloor .
\]
The handle certifies that \(2\le K_n\) whenever \(0<n\), \(0<d\), \(N\le n\), and \(d\le \rho nL\).  The active branch below is used on \(N\le n\) and \(d\le \rho nL\); the calibrated value is \(T_n^{\mathrm{poly}}=0\) when \(N>n\) or \(d>\rho nL\).

\begin{enumerate}
\item Split the sample into the pilot and estimation blocks
\[
I_0:=\{1,\ldots,\lfloor n/2\rfloor\},
\qquad
I_1:=\{\lfloor n/2\rfloor+1,\ldots,n\},
\qquad
m_1:=|I_1|=n-\lfloor n/2\rfloor .
\]

\item Use \(I_0\) to form the empirically heavy and light cell sets
\[
\widehat{\mathcal H}
:=
\left\{k:256L<\sum_{i\in I_0}\mathbf 1\{X_i=k\}\right\},
\qquad
\widehat{\mathcal L}
:=
\{1,\ldots,d\}\setminus \widehat{\mathcal H}.
\]

\item On each heavy cell \(k\in\widehat{\mathcal H}\), use \(I_1\) to compute the estimation-block arm counts, cell count, arm outcome totals, totalized arm means, and normalized plug-in contribution
\[
N_{ak}^{(1)}
:=
\sum_{i\in I_1}\mathbf 1\{X_i=k,A_i=a\},
\qquad
N_k^{(1)}
:=
\sum_{i\in I_1}\mathbf 1\{X_i=k\},
\]
\[
S_{ak}^{(1)}
:=
\sum_{i\in I_1}\mathbf 1\{X_i=k,A_i=a\}Y_i,
\qquad
\overline Y_{ak}^{(1)}
:=
\begin{cases}
S_{ak}^{(1)}/N_{ak}^{(1)}, & N_{ak}^{(1)}>0,\\
0, & N_{ak}^{(1)}=0,
\end{cases}
\]
\[
\widehat h_k
:=
\frac{N_k^{(1)}}{m_1}\,
\frac{\overline Y_{1k}^{(1)}-\overline Y_{0k}^{(1)}}{M}.
\]

\item On each light cell \(k\in\widehat{\mathcal L}\), set
\[
B:=\frac{4096L}{m_1},
\qquad
g_{K_n,j}:=
(-1)^j\frac{2^{2j+3}}{K_n(K_n+j+2)}{K_n+j+2\choose 2j+4},
\qquad
j=0,\ldots,K_n-2.
\]
With \((m)_r\) denoting the falling factorial, evaluate the ordered distinct-index one-mark statistic
\[
U_{k,a,j}
:=
\frac{1}{(m_1)_{j+2}}
\sum_{\substack{(i_0,\ldots,i_{j+1})\in I_1^{j+2}\\
i_0,\ldots,i_{j+1}\ \mathrm{distinct}}}
\frac{Y_{i_0}}{M}\,
\mathbf 1\{X_{i_0}=k,A_{i_0}=a\}
\left(\prod_{\ell=1}^{j}\mathbf 1\{X_{i_\ell}=k,A_{i_\ell}=a\}\right)
\mathbf 1\{X_{i_{j+1}}=k\},
\]
and set the normalized light-cell contribution to
\[
\widehat P_k
:=
\sum_{a\in\{0,1\}}(-1)^{1-a}
\sum_{j=0}^{K_n-2}\frac{g_{K_n,j}}{B^{j+1}}U_{k,a,j}.
\]

\item Writing \(\operatorname{clip}_{[a,b]}(x):=\min\{b,\max\{a,x\}\}\) for truncation to the interval \([a,b]\), sum the heavy and light contributions and output the clipped active-branch statistic
\[
T_n^{\mathrm{poly}}
:=
M\operatorname{clip}_{[-1,1]}
\left(
\sum_{k\in\widehat{\mathcal H}}\widehat h_k
+
\sum_{k\in\widehat{\mathcal L}}\widehat P_k
\right).
\]
\end{enumerate}

blocks.title: Collision estimator \(T_n^{\mathrm{col}}\)
blocks.body:
For observations \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\), define \(T_n^{\mathrm{col}}\) by the following one-pass cell aggregation followed by one pass through the occupied categories.

\begin{enumerate}
\item For each arm \(a\in\{0,1\}\) and cell \(k\in\{1,\ldots,d\}\), define the full-sample arm-cell count and outcome total
\[
N_{ak}
:=
\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{X_i=k,A_i=a\},
\qquad
S_{ak}
:=
\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf 1\{X_i=k,A_i=a\}Y_i.
\]

\item Define the full-sample cell count, crossed-cell indicator, and total count in empirically crossed cells
\[
N_k:=N_{0k}+N_{1k},
\qquad
I_k:=\mathbf 1\{N_{0k}N_{1k}>0\},
\qquad
R_n:=\sum_{k=1}^d N_k I_k.
\]

\item For positive arm-cell counts, define the arm-cell sample means
\[
\overline Y_{ak}:=\frac{S_{ak}}{N_{ak}}
\qquad\text{when }N_{ak}>0.
\]

\item Output the occupancy-weighted treated-control statistic
\[
T_n^{\mathrm{col}}
:=
\operatorname{clip}_{[-M,M]}
\left(
\frac{\mathbf 1\{R_n>0\}}{R_n}
\sum_{k=1}^d
N_kI_k(\overline Y_{1k}-\overline Y_{0k})
\right),
\]
where the inner value is \(0\) when \(R_n=0\).
\end{enumerate}

blocks.title: Selector \(\widehat\tau_n^{\star}\)
blocks.body:
Given candidate estimators \(T_n^{\mathrm{poly}}\) and \(T_n^{\mathrm{col}}\), each a total measurable map \(\mathcal O^n\to[-M,M]\), define \(\widehat\tau_n^{\star}\) by the following steps.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Define the rare-cell polynomial remainder
\[
u_{n,d}:=\frac{d^2}{n^2\log^2(en)}.
\]
\item Define the collision remainder
\[
h_{n,d,\sigma}:=\sigma^2+\frac{d}{n^2}.
\]
\item Output the measurable selector
\[
\widehat\tau_n^{\star}:=
\begin{cases}
T_n^{\mathrm{col}},&h_{n,d,\sigma}\le\min\{1,u_{n,d}\},\\
T_n^{\mathrm{poly}},&u_{n,d}<\min\{1,h_{n,d,\sigma}\},\\
0,&\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\]
\end{enumerate}

blocks.title: Least-favorable handle
blocks.body:
For fixed constants \(b_{\epsilon}^{\mathrm{rad}},b_{\epsilon}^{\mathrm{ex}}>0\) depending only on \(\epsilon\), define the two embedded hard families and the channel as follows.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Set the channel attenuation
\[
\lambda:=\frac{\sigma}{2}.
\]
\item For the radius component, set the capped alphabet size
\[
d_{\mathrm{rad}}:=\min\{d,\max(1,\lfloor b_{\epsilon}^{\mathrm{rad}}n\log(en)\rfloor)\}.
\]
Start from a fixed-sample binary one-arm hard family with at most \(d_{\mathrm{rad}}\) positive-mass cells, and assign zero mass to unused cells.
\item Pass each binary potential response through the hypothesis-independent channel
\[
B'(a)\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}\!\left\{\frac12+\lambda\left(B(a)-\frac12\right)\right\},
\]
and define the scaled real potential response
\[
Y(a):=M\{B'(a)-1/2\}.
\]
\item For the exact-homogeneity component, set the capped alphabet size
\[
d_{\mathrm{ex}}:=\min\{d,\max(1,\lfloor b_{\epsilon}^{\mathrm{ex}}n^2\rfloor)\}.
\]
Start from a uniform-mass binary hard family on at most \(d_{\mathrm{ex}}\) positive-mass cells, assign zero mass to unused cells, and define
\[
Y(a):=M\{B(a)-1/2\}.
\]
\item The construction outputs the radius-channel embedded family, the exact-homogeneity embedded family, and the channel above.
\end{enumerate}

blocks.title: Minimax risk \(\mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}\) and estimator class \(\mathcal T_{n,M}\)
ATE g-formula identification
blocks.body:
For every dimension \(d\), overlap parameter \(\epsilon\), envelope level \(M\), radius \(\sigma\), and every \(P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}\) in the sense of \cref{obj:def:model-class}, the average treatment effect functional \(\tau(P)\) of \cref{obj:def:ate-functional} equals the full-data causal contrast and is identified from the observed margin by the finite-cell g-formula:
\[
\tau(P)
=
\int \{Y(1)-Y(0)\}\,dP
=
\sum_{k=1}^{d} p_k
\left\{
E_P[Y\mid A=1,X=k]-E_P[Y\mid A=0,X=k]
\right\}.
\]

blocks.title: Scale sanity
blocks.body:
For any \(d\in\mathbb N\) and any \(\epsilon,M\in\mathbb R\), let \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}^{\mathrm{unr}}\) and \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}\) be the model classes in \cref{obj:def:unrestricted-class,obj:def:model-class}. For each law \(P\), write
\[
\tau_k(P)=\mu_{1k}(P)-\mu_{0k}(P),
\qquad
\tau(P)=\sum_{k\in\{1,\ldots,d\}} p_k(P)\tau_k(P),
\qquad
\delta_k(P)=\tau_k(P)-\tau(P).
\]
Every \(P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}^{\mathrm{unr}}\) satisfies
\[
|\tau_k(P)|\le M\quad\text{for every }k\text{ with }p_k(P)>0,
\qquad
|\tau(P)|\le M,
\]
and
\[
|\delta_k(P)|\le 2M\quad\text{for every }k\text{ with }p_k(P)>0.
\]
Consequently the two classes have the same underlying laws at radius \(2\): for every \(P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}^{\mathrm{unr}}\) there exists \(Q\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,2}\) with the same law as \(P\), and for every \(Q\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,2}\) there exists \(P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}^{\mathrm{unr}}\) with the same law as \(Q\).

blocks.title: Restricted frontier upper bound
blocks.body:
For every overlap parameter \(\epsilon\) with \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), there exist constants \(C_{\epsilon},c_{\epsilon}>0\) and a polynomial calibration handle \((N,\rho)\) with \(\rho>0\) such that, for all positive integers \(n,d\),
\[
N\le n
\quad\text{and}\quad
d\le \rho n\log(en)
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
2\le K_n ,
\]
where \(K_n\) is the active polynomial degree in the polynomial estimator.  For every \(n,d,M,\sigma\), assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Sample and alphabet.)} \(n\ge1\) and \(d\ge1\).
\item \textbf{(Envelope and radius.)} \(M\ge1\) and \(0\le\sigma\le2\).
\item \textbf{(Restricted dimension.)}
\[
d\le c_{\epsilon}\frac{n^2}{\log(en)} .
\]
\end{itemize}
Let \(T_n^{\mathrm{poly}}\in\mathcal T_{n,M}\) be the polynomial estimator determined by this handle, let \(T_n^{\mathrm{col}}\in\mathcal T_{n,M}\) be the collision estimator, and let \(\widehat\tau_n^{\star}\) be the known-radius selector of \cref{obj:def:total-estimator} applied to \(T_n^{\mathrm{poly}}\), \(T_n^{\mathrm{col}}\), and \(\sigma\).  Put
\[
r_{n,d,\sigma}
=
\frac1n+
\min\left\{
1,\,
\min\left\{
\frac{d^2}{n^2\log^2(en)},\,
\sigma^2+\frac{d}{n^2}
\right\}
\right\}.
\]
Then \(\widehat\tau_n^{\star}\in\mathcal T_{n,M}\), and for every \(P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}\) in \cref{obj:def:model-class},
\[
E_{Q_P^{(n)}}\!\left[
\left(\widehat\tau_n^{\star}-\tau(P)\right)^2
\right]
\le
C_{\epsilon}M^2 r_{n,d,\sigma}.
\]

blocks.title: Parametric minimax lower bound
Endpoint rate reductions
blocks.body:
For every overlap parameter \(\epsilon\in(0,1/2)\), there exist constants \(c_\epsilon,c,C\in\mathbb R\) such that
\[
0<c_\epsilon\le 1,
\qquad
0<c\le C .
\]
Write
\[
L_n=\log(en),
\qquad
u_{n,d}=\frac{d^2}{n^2L_n^2}.
\]
Then the following statements hold.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Exact-homogeneity endpoint.)} For all integers \(n,d\ge1\) such that
\[
d\le c_\epsilon\,\frac{n^2}{L_n},
\]
the upper-frontier expression
\[
\frac1n+\min\left\{1,\min\left\{u_{n,d},\frac d{n^2}\right\}\right\}
\]
and the capped converse expression
\[
\frac1n+\min\left\{1,\frac d{n^2}\right\}
\]
are both comparable to \(n^{-1}+d/n^2\):
\[
c\left(\frac1n+\frac d{n^2}\right)
\le
\frac1n+\min\left\{1,\min\left\{u_{n,d},\frac d{n^2}\right\}\right\}
\le
C\left(\frac1n+\frac d{n^2}\right),
\]
and
\[
c\left(\frac1n+\frac d{n^2}\right)
\le
\frac1n+\min\left\{1,\frac d{n^2}\right\}
\le
C\left(\frac1n+\frac d{n^2}\right).
\]
\item \textbf{(Radius-two class identity.)} For every integer \(d\) and every \(M\in\mathbb R\), the radius-two class in \cref{obj:def:model-class} and the unrestricted class in \cref{obj:def:unrestricted-class} have exactly the same attainable laws: every law in \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}^{\mathrm{unr}}\) is the law of some member of \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,2}\), and every law in \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,2}\) is the law of some member of \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}^{\mathrm{unr}}\).
\item \textbf{(Radius-two endpoint.)} For all integers \(n,d\ge1\), the upper-frontier expression at radius two is exactly
\[
\frac1n+\min\{1,u_{n,d}\},
\]
and the capped converse expression at radius two,
\[
\frac1n+\min\left\{1,\frac d{n^2}\right\}+4\min\{1,u_{n,d}\},
\]
is comparable to the same rate:
\[
c\left(\frac1n+\min\{1,u_{n,d}\}\right)
\le
\frac1n+\min\left\{1,\frac d{n^2}\right\}+4\min\{1,u_{n,d}\}
\le
C\left(\frac1n+\min\{1,u_{n,d}\}\right).
\]
\end{itemize}

blocks.title: Binary one-arm lower bound
blocks.body:
For every real overlap constant \(\epsilon\), if \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), then there exist constants \(a_{\epsilon},b_{\epsilon}>0\) and an integer \(N_{\epsilon}\) such that the following holds.  For every sample size \(n\) and alphabet size \(d\),
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Positive alphabet.)} \(d\ge 1\).
\item \textbf{(Large sample.)} \(n\ge N_{\epsilon}\).
\item \textbf{(Source range.)} \(d\le b_{\epsilon}n\log n\).
\end{itemize}
In the fixed-sample binary observed-data experiment with observations \((X,A,Y)\in\{1,\ldots,d\}\times\{0,1\}\times\{0,1\}\), arbitrary cell masses \(p_k=P(X=k)\), product sampling law \(P^{\otimes n}\), overlap
\[
\epsilon\le P(A=1\mid X=k)\le 1-\epsilon
\]
on every positive-mass category, and identically zero control-arm response mean \(E_P[Y\mid A=0,X=k]=0\), the treated-arm minimax risk satisfies
\[
\inf_{\widehat\psi}
\sup_P
E_{P^{\otimes n}}\left[
\left\{\widehat\psi-\sum_{k=1}^d p_k E_P[Y\mid A=1,X=k]\right\}^2
\right]
\ge
a_{\epsilon}
\left\{
\frac{1}{n}
+
\frac{d^2}{n^2(\log n)^2}
\right\},
\]
where the infimum is over measurable estimators of the fixed sample.

blocks.title: Usable occupancy reciprocal
blocks.body:
For every overlap parameter \(\epsilon\in\mathbb R\), there are constants
\(b_{\epsilon},B_{\epsilon}>0\), depending only on \(\epsilon\), such that the following holds.
For every \(n,d\in\mathbb N\), every \(M,\sigma\in\mathbb R\), and every
\(P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}\), let \(Q_P^{(n)}\) denote the \(n\)-fold observed-data law and define
\[
N_{ak}:=\sum_{i=1}^n \mathbf 1\{X_i=k,A_i=a\},\qquad
N_k:=N_{0k}+N_{1k},\qquad
I_k:=\mathbf 1\{N_{0k}>0,\ N_{1k}>0\},
\]
with
\[
R_n:=\sum_{k=1}^d N_k I_k .
\]
Then
\[
Q_P^{(n)}(R_n=0)
\le
2\exp\left\{-b_{\epsilon}\frac{n^2}{n\vee d}\right\},
\]
and
\[
E_{Q_P^{(n)}}\left[
\mathbf 1\{R_n>0\}\frac{1}{R_n}
\right]
\le
B_{\epsilon}\left\{
\frac{n\vee d}{n^2}
+
\exp\left(-b_{\epsilon}\frac{n^2}{n\vee d}\right)
\right\}.
\]

blocks.title: Radius-channel hard-family embedding
blocks.body:
For \(0\le\sigma\le2\), set \(\lambda:=\sigma/2\). The embedding \(\Psi\) sends a binary source law from the radius-channel hard family, after padding unused cells with zero mass in the \(d\)-alphabet, to the real-outcome law obtained by the hypothesis-independent channel
\[
B(a)\longmapsto B'(a)\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}\!\left\{\frac12+\lambda\left(B(a)-\frac12\right)\right\},
\qquad
Y(a):=M\{B'(a)-1/2\},
\qquad
Y=Y(A).
\]
For source laws \(P_0\) and \(P_1\) in the realized family, the embedded targets satisfy
\[
\tau(\Psi(P_1))-\tau(\Psi(P_0))
=
M\frac{\sigma}{2}\{\psi(P_1)-\psi(P_0)\}.
\]

blocks.title: Radius-channel converse
blocks.body:
For every overlap parameter \(\epsilon\) satisfying \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), there exist constants \(c_{\epsilon}\) and \(b_{\epsilon}^{\mathrm{rad}}\) such that
\[
0<c_{\epsilon}\le 1,
\qquad
0<b_{\epsilon}^{\mathrm{rad}}.
\]
For every \(n,d\in\mathbb N\), \(M\in\mathbb R\), and \(\sigma\in\mathbb R\), suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Sample and alphabet.)} \(0<n\) and \(0<d\).
\item \textbf{(Scale and radius.)} \(1\le M\) and \(0\le\sigma\le2\).
\item \textbf{(Restricted range.)}
\[
d\le c_{\epsilon}\frac{n^2}{\log(en)}.
\]
\end{itemize}
Then the minimax risk from \cref{obj:def:minimax-risk} satisfies
\[
\mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}
\ge
c_{\epsilon}M^2
\left\{
\frac1n+\frac d{n^2}
+\sigma^2
\min\left(1,\frac{d^2}{n^2\log^2(en)}\right)
\right\}.
\]
Moreover, the radius-channel hard family can be realized with the same constants: there are an integer cap, a source class, a padding map into the \(d\)-alphabet, an embedding \(\Psi\) of the source laws into real-outcome laws, and a coupling for the binary full-observation experiment such that the realized radial-channel data have radius parameter \(b_{\epsilon}^{\mathrm{rad}}\), and for all source laws \(P_0\) and \(P_1\),
\[
\tau(\Psi(P_1))-\tau(\Psi(P_0))
=
M\frac{\sigma}{2}
\left\{\psi(P_1)-\psi(P_0)\right\}.
\]
For every total measurable \([-M,M]\)-valued estimator \(\widehat\tau\), some source law \(P\) in this realized family satisfies
\[
c_{\epsilon}M^2\sigma^2
\min\left(1,\frac{d^2}{n^2\log^2(en)}\right)
\le
\mathbb E_{\Psi(P)}
\left[
\left\{\widehat\tau-\tau(\Psi(P))\right\}^2
\right].
\]

blocks.title: Robust upper construction
blocks.body:
For every overlap parameter \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), there exist constants \(C_{\epsilon},c_{\epsilon}>0\) and a calibrated polynomial handle consisting of a cutoff \(N\) and an active-range multiplier \(\rho>0\) such that, for every \(n,d\ge 1\),
\[
N\le n,\qquad d\le \rho n\log(en)
\]
implies that the associated polynomial degree is at least \(2\). For every \(n,d\ge 1\), \(M\ge 1\), and \(0\le \sigma\le 2\), the handle-indexed polynomial estimator \(T_n^{\mathrm{poly}}\) and the occupancy-weighted estimator \(T_n^{\mathrm{col}}\) of \cref{obj:def:collision-handle} are measurable functions of the sample and take values in \([-M,M]\).

If, in addition,
\[
d\le c_{\epsilon}\frac{n^2}{\log(en)},
\]
then for every \(P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}\) as defined in \cref{obj:def:model-class},
\[
E_{Q_P^{(n)}}\!\left[\left(T_n^{\mathrm{poly}}-\tau(P)\right)^2\right]
\le
C_{\epsilon}M^2
\left\{
\frac1n+\min\left(1,\frac{d^2}{n^2\log^2(en)}\right)
\right\},
\]
and
\[
E_{Q_P^{(n)}}\!\left[\left(T_n^{\mathrm{col}}-\tau(P)\right)^2\right]
\le
C_{\epsilon}M^2
\left(
\frac1n+\sigma^2+\frac{d}{n^2}
\right).
\]

blocks.title: Fixed-interior gap characterization
blocks.body:
For every overlap parameter \(\epsilon\) with \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), there is a constant \(c_\epsilon>0\) such that the following statements hold.  Write
\[
L_n:=\log(en),\qquad
b_{n,d}:=\frac1n+\frac d{n^2},\qquad
u_{n,d}:=\frac{d^2}{n^2L_n^2},
\]
and
\[
q_{n,d,\sigma}:=\frac1n+\min\left\{u_{n,d},\,\sigma^2+\frac d{n^2}\right\},
\qquad
\ell_{n,d,\sigma}:=b_{n,d}+\sigma^2u_{n,d}.
\]
Also let \(r_{n,d,\sigma}\) denote the frontier rate
\[
r_{n,d,\sigma}:=\frac1n+\min\left\{1,\,\min\{u_{n,d},\,\left(\sigma^2+\frac d{n^2}\right)\}\right\},
\]
and let \(\mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}\) be the minimax mean-squared risk in \cref{obj:def:minimax-risk}.

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Triangular benchmark algebra.)}  For all \(n,d\in\mathbb N\) and all \(\sigma\in[0,2]\), if
\[
L_n^2<d<nL_n,
\]
then
\[
\frac12\left\{b_{n,d}+\min(u_{n,d},\sigma^2)\right\}
\le q_{n,d,\sigma}
\le b_{n,d}+\min(u_{n,d},\sigma^2),
\qquad
\ell_{n,d,\sigma}=b_{n,d}+\sigma^2u_{n,d}.
\]

\item \textbf{(Fixed interior radii.)}  For every \(\underline\sigma\in(0,2]\), there are constants \(c,C\) with \(0<c\le C\) such that, for all \(n,d\in\mathbb N\) and \(M,\sigma\in\mathbb R\), if
\[
n>0,\qquad d>0,\qquad M\ge1,\qquad
\underline\sigma\le\sigma\le2,\qquad
d\le c_\epsilon\frac{n^2}{L_n},
\]
then
\[
cM^2r_{n,d,\sigma}
\le
\mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}
\le
CM^2r_{n,d,\sigma}.
\]

\item \textbf{(Matching elbows.)}  For every \(K\ge0\), there are constants \(c,C\) with \(0<c\le C\) such that, for all \(n,d\in\mathbb N\) and \(M,\sigma\in\mathbb R\), if
\[
n>0,\qquad d>0,\qquad M\ge1,\qquad 0\le\sigma\le2,
\]
and at least one of
\[
u_{n,d}\ge1,\qquad
u_{n,d}\le Kb_{n,d},\qquad
\sigma^2\le Kb_{n,d}
\]
holds, then
\[
cM^2r_{n,d,\sigma}
\le
\mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}
\le
CM^2r_{n,d,\sigma}.
\]

\item \textbf{(Exact algebraic elbow.)}  For all \(n,d\in\mathbb N\) with \(n>0\),
\[
u_{n,d}\le b_{n,d}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
d^2\le nL_n^2+dL_n^2.
\]

\item \textbf{(Residual wedge implication.)}  For every alphabet sequence \(d_t\) and radius sequence \(\sigma_t\), if eventually
\[
d_t\ge1,\qquad 0\le\sigma_t\le2,
\]
and
\[
\frac{r_{t,d_t,\sigma_t}}{t^{-1}+\min\{1,d_t/t^2\}+\sigma_t^2\min\{1,u_{t,d_t}\}}\longrightarrow\infty,
\]
then the sequence lies in the residual wedge:
\[
\frac{b_{t,d_t}}{u_{t,d_t}}\longrightarrow0,\qquad
u_{t,d_t}\longrightarrow0,\qquad
\frac{b_{t,d_t}}{\sigma_t^2}\longrightarrow0,\qquad
\sigma_t^2\longrightarrow0.
\]

\item \textbf{(Witness sequence.)}  The sequence \(d_n=n\) and \(\sigma_n=L_n^{-1/2}\) lies in the residual wedge.  Along this sequence,
\[
\frac{q_{n,n,L_n^{-1/2}}}{\ell_{n,n,L_n^{-1/2}}}
\asymp L_n,
\qquad
\frac{q_{n,n,L_n^{-1/2}}}{\ell_{n,n,L_n^{-1/2}}}\longrightarrow\infty .
\]
\end{itemize}

blocks.title: Two-sided minimax bracket
Continuous occupancy collision bound
blocks.body:
For every overlap parameter \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), there is a constant \(C_{\epsilon}>0\) such that the following holds.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Sample size and alphabet.)} The integers \(n\) and \(d\) satisfy \(n\ge 1\) and \(d\ge 1\).
\item \textbf{(Model.)} The distribution \(P\) belongs to \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}\) from \cref{obj:def:model-class}, with its corresponding bounds on \(M\) and \(\sigma\).
\item \textbf{(Estimator.)} The estimator is the clipped occupancy-weighted treated-control estimator \(T_n^{\mathrm{col}}\) defined in \cref{obj:def:collision-handle} with clipping level \(M\).
\end{itemize}
Then
\[
  E_{Q_P^{(n)}}\!\left[\left(T_n^{\mathrm{col}}-\tau(P)\right)^2\right]
  \le
  C_{\epsilon}M^2
  \left(
    \frac{1}{n}
    +\sigma^2
    +\frac{d}{n^2}
  \right).
\]

blocks.title: Scaled binary lower transfer
All-alphabet upper construction
blocks.body:
For every \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), there exist a constant \(C_\epsilon>0\) and a polynomial calibration handle \(h=(N,\rho)\) with \(\rho>0\) such that, for every \(n,d\ge 1\), every \(M\ge 1\), and every \(0\le \sigma\le 2\), the following hold:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Polynomial calibration.)} The handle satisfies \(N\le n\) and \(d\le \rho n\log(en)\Rightarrow 2\le K_n\), where \(K_n\) is the polynomial degree used by the handle-indexed heavy-light signed one-mark Chebyshev factorial estimator \(T_n^{\mathrm{poly}}\).
\item \textbf{(Admissibility.)} The estimators \(T_n^{\mathrm{poly}}\) and \(T_n^{\mathrm{col}}\), with \(T_n^{\mathrm{col}}\) as in \cref{obj:def:collision-handle}, are measurable maps of the \(n\)-sample and take values in \([-M,M]\).
\item \textbf{(Model class.)} The risk bounds are uniform over \(P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}\), the model class in \cref{obj:def:model-class}.
\end{itemize}
With \(u_{n,d}=d^2/\{n^2\log^2(en)\}\), the estimators obey
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}}
E_{Q_P^{(n)}}\!\left[\{T_n^{\mathrm{poly}}-\tau(P)\}^2\right]
\le
C_\epsilon M^2\left\{\frac1n+\min(1,u_{n,d})\right\}
\]
and
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}}
E_{Q_P^{(n)}}\!\left[\{T_n^{\mathrm{col}}-\tau(P)\}^2\right]
\le
C_\epsilon M^2\left(\frac1n+\sigma^2+\frac{d}{n^2}\right).
\]

blocks.title: All-alphabet frontier upper bound
blocks.body:
For every overlap parameter \(\epsilon\) with \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), there exist a constant \(C_{\epsilon}>0\) and a polynomial calibration handle \((N_{\epsilon},\rho_{\epsilon})\) such that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Handle calibration.)} \(\rho_{\epsilon}>0\), and for every pair of integers \(n,d\ge1\),
\[
N_{\epsilon}\le n,\qquad d\le \rho_{\epsilon} n\log(en)
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
2\le K_n ,
\]
where \(K_n\) is the polynomial degree used by the polynomial estimator.
\item \textbf{(Index range.)} The guarantee applies to every pair of integers \(n,d\ge1\), every \(M\ge1\), and every \(0\le\sigma\le2\).
\item \textbf{(Model class.)} The law \(P\) ranges over \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}\) from \cref{obj:def:model-class}.
\end{itemize}
For these indices, let \(T_n^{\mathrm{poly}}\) be the admissible polynomial estimator calibrated by \((N_{\epsilon},\rho_{\epsilon})\), let \(T_n^{\mathrm{col}}\) be the collision estimator, and let \(\widehat\tau_n^{\star}\) be the known-radius selector in \cref{obj:def:total-estimator} applied with radius \(\sigma\) to these two estimators, and write
\[
r_{n,d,\sigma}
=
\frac{1}{n}
+
\min\left\{
1,\,
\min\left[
\frac{d^2}{n^2\log^2(en)},\,
\sigma^2+\frac{d}{n^2}
\right]
\right\}
\]
for the selector benchmark. Then \(\widehat\tau_n^{\star}\) is measurable, satisfies \(\widehat\tau_n^{\star}(s)\in[-M,M]\) for every sample \(s\), and
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}}
E_{Q_P^{(n)}}\!\left[\left(\widehat\tau_n^{\star}-\tau(P)\right)^2\right]
\le
C_{\epsilon}M^2 r_{n,d,\sigma}.
\]

blocks.title: Endpoint rate reductions
blocks.body:
There exist constants \(c,C\in(0,\infty)\), with \(c\le C\), such that the following hold.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Exact homogeneity.)} For every pair of integers \(n,d\ge 1\),
\[
c\left\{n^{-1}+\min\left(1,\frac d{n^2}\right)\right\}
\le
n^{-1}+\min\left\{1,\frac{d^2}{n^2\log^2(en)},\frac d{n^2}\right\}
\le
C\left\{n^{-1}+\min\left(1,\frac d{n^2}\right)\right\},
\]
and
\[
c\left\{n^{-1}+\min\left(1,\frac d{n^2}\right)\right\}
\le
n^{-1}+\min\left(1,\frac d{n^2}\right)
\le
C\left\{n^{-1}+\min\left(1,\frac d{n^2}\right)\right\}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Unrestricted radius.)} For every pair of integers \(n,d\ge 1\),
\[
c\left\{n^{-1}+\min\left(1,\frac{d^2}{n^2\log^2(en)}\right)\right\}
\le
n^{-1}+\min\left(1,\frac{d^2}{n^2\log^2(en)}\right)
\le
C\left\{n^{-1}+\min\left(1,\frac{d^2}{n^2\log^2(en)}\right)\right\},
\]
and
\[
c\left\{n^{-1}+\min\left(1,\frac{d^2}{n^2\log^2(en)}\right)\right\}
\le
n^{-1}+\min\left(1,\frac d{n^2}\right)
+4\min\left(1,\frac{d^2}{n^2\log^2(en)}\right)
\le
C\left\{n^{-1}+\min\left(1,\frac{d^2}{n^2\log^2(en)}\right)\right\}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Class equality at radius two.)} For every alphabet size \(d\), every \(\epsilon\in\mathbb R\), and every \(M\in\mathbb R\), the laws represented by \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}^{\mathrm{unr}}\) in \cref{obj:def:unrestricted-class} are exactly the laws represented by \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,2}\) in \cref{obj:def:model-class}.
\item \textbf{(Endpoint identity.)} For every pair of integers \(n,d\ge 1\), the radius-two upper frontier expression is exactly
\[
n^{-1}+\min\left(1,\frac{d^2}{n^2\log^2(en)}\right).
\]
\end{itemize}

blocks.title: Fixed-radius wedge characterization
blocks.body:
Fix \(0<\epsilon<1/2\).  For \(n,d\in\mathbb N\), put \(L_n=\log(en)\),
\[
b_{n,d}=\frac1n+\frac d{n^2},
\qquad
u_{n,d}=\frac{d^2}{n^2L_n^2},
\qquad
h_{n,d,\sigma}=\sigma^2+\frac d{n^2},
\qquad
r_{n,d,\sigma}=\frac1n+\min\{1,\min(u_{n,d},h_{n,d,\sigma})\},
\]
and define
\[
q_{n,d,\sigma}=\frac1n+\min\left\{u_{n,d},\sigma^2+\frac d{n^2}\right\},
\qquad
\ell_{n,d,\sigma}=b_{n,d}+\sigma^2u_{n,d}.
\]
Let \(\mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}\) be the minimax mean-squared risk in \cref{obj:def:minimax-risk}.  Then all of the following hold.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Triangular benchmarks.)} For every \(n,d\in\mathbb N\) and every \(0\le\sigma\le2\), if
\[
L_n^2<d<nL_n,
\]
then
\[
\frac12\{b_{n,d}+\min(u_{n,d},\sigma^2)\}
\le q_{n,d,\sigma}
\le b_{n,d}+\min(u_{n,d},\sigma^2),
\qquad
\ell_{n,d,\sigma}=b_{n,d}+\sigma^2u_{n,d}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Fixed interior radii.)} For every \(\underline\sigma\in(0,2]\), there exist constants \(c,C\) with \(0<c\le C\) such that, for every \(n,d\in\mathbb N\), every \(M\ge1\), and every \(\sigma\) satisfying \(\underline\sigma\le\sigma\le2\),
\[
cM^2r_{n,d,\sigma}
\le
\mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}
\le
CM^2r_{n,d,\sigma},
\]
whenever \(n\ge1\) and \(d\ge1\).
\item \textbf{(Matching elbows.)} For every \(K\ge0\), there exist constants \(c,C\) with \(0<c\le C\) such that, for every \(n,d\in\mathbb N\), every \(M\ge1\), and every \(0\le\sigma\le2\),
\[
cM^2r_{n,d,\sigma}
\le
\mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}
\le
CM^2r_{n,d,\sigma},
\]
whenever \(n\ge1\), \(d\ge1\), and at least one of
\[
1\le u_{n,d},
\qquad
u_{n,d}\le Kb_{n,d},
\qquad
\sigma^2\le Kb_{n,d}
\]
holds.
\item \textbf{(Exact algebraic elbow.)} For every \(n,d\in\mathbb N\) with \(n\ge1\),
\[
u_{n,d}\le b_{n,d}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
d^2\le nL_n^2+dL_n^2.
\]
\item \textbf{(Sufficient elbows.)} For every \(n,d\in\mathbb N\) with \(n\ge1\),
\[
d\le\sqrt n\,L_n \quad\Longrightarrow\quad u_{n,d}\le b_{n,d},
\]
and
\[
d\le L_n^2 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad u_{n,d}\le b_{n,d}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Residual wedge implication.)} For any sequences \(d_n\in\mathbb N\) and \(\sigma_n\in\mathbb R\), if eventually \(d_n\ge1\) and \(0\le\sigma_n\le2\), and if the frontier-to-capped-converse benchmark ratio
\[
\frac{r_{n,d_n,\sigma_n}}
{n^{-1}+\min\{1,d_n/n^2\}+\sigma_n^2\min\{1,u_{n,d_n}\}}
\to\infty,
\]
then the sequence lies in the residual wedge:
\[
\frac{b_{n,d_n}}{u_{n,d_n}}\to0,
\qquad
u_{n,d_n}\to0,
\qquad
\frac{b_{n,d_n}}{\sigma_n^2}\to0,
\qquad
\sigma_n^2\to0.
\]
\item \textbf{(Nonempty wedge.)} The sequence \(d_n=n\) and \(\sigma_n=L_n^{-1/2}\) lies in the residual wedge.
\item \textbf{(Diagonal divergence.)} Along \(d_n=n\) and \(\sigma_n=L_n^{-1/2}\),
\[
\frac{q_{n,n,L_n^{-1/2}}}{\ell_{n,n,L_n^{-1/2}}}
\asymp L_n
\]
eventually, and
\[
\frac{q_{n,n,L_n^{-1/2}}}{\ell_{n,n,L_n^{-1/2}}}\to\infty .
\]
\end{itemize}

blocks.title: All-alphabet minimax bracket
blocks.body:
For every overlap parameter \(\epsilon\) with \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), there are real constants \(c_{\epsilon}\) and \(C_{\epsilon}\) such that
\[
0<c_{\epsilon}\le 1,\qquad 1\le C_{\epsilon},\qquad c_{\epsilon}\le C_{\epsilon}.
\]
For every \(n,d\in\mathbb N\), \(M\in\mathbb R\), and \(\sigma\in\mathbb R\), suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Sample and alphabet sizes.)} \(n\ge 1\) and \(d\ge 1\).
\item \textbf{(Outcome envelope.)} \(M\ge 1\).
\item \textbf{(Radius range.)} \(0\le \sigma\le 2\).
\end{itemize}
Let \(\mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}\) be the minimax mean-squared risk in \cref{obj:def:minimax-risk} over the real-outcome class \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}\) with fixed overlap \(\epsilon\), conditional exchangeability, consistency, conditional mean normalization, conditional second central moment envelope \(M\), and approximate-homogeneity radius \(\sigma M\). Define
\[
u_{n,d}=\frac{d^2}{n^2\log^2(en)},
\qquad
h_{n,d,\sigma}=\sigma^2+\frac{d}{n^2},
\]
and write
\[
\ell_{n,d,\sigma}
=
\frac{1}{n}
+
\min\left\{1,\frac{d}{n^2}\right\}
+
\sigma^2\min\left\{1,u_{n,d}\right\},
\qquad
r_{n,d,\sigma}
=
\frac{1}{n}
+
\min\left\{1,u_{n,d},h_{n,d,\sigma}\right\}.
\]
Then
\[
c_{\epsilon}M^2\ell_{n,d,\sigma}
\le
\mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}
\le
C_{\epsilon}M^2r_{n,d,\sigma}.
\]

blocks.title: Shrinking-radius frontier
blocks.body:
Let
\[
L:=\log(en),\qquad
b:=n^{-1}+\frac{d}{n^2},\qquad
u:=\frac{d^2}{n^2L^2}.
\]
In the residual shrinking-radius wedge
\[
b\ll u\ll1,
\qquad
b\ll\sigma^2\ll1,
\]
equivalently up to boundary constants
\[
\sqrt n\,L\ll d\ll nL,
\qquad
\sigma^2\gg b,
\]
a natural next question is whether one can either construct a realization-wise radius-constrained paired-cell moment-matching fuzzy experiment in \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}\) with ATE separation of order
\[
M\min\left\{\sigma,\frac{d}{nL}\right\}
\]
and sample-mixture total variation bounded away from one, or construct an explicit total estimator whose risk is strictly smaller in order than the selector benchmark
\[
M^2\{b+\min(u,\sigma^2)\},
\]
with the product benchmark
\[
M^2(b+\sigma^2u)
\]
as the target rate. The hypothesis-independent channel yields the product separation
\[
M\sigma\min\left\{1,\frac{d}{nL}\right\}.
\]

blocks.title: Binary collision comparison
blocks.body:
Fix \(\epsilon\in(0,1/2)\).  For a binary \(d\)-cell law \(P\) write \(P_n\) for its \(n\)-sample product experiment and \(s\) for the published binary occupancy-weighted collision estimator, and say that \(P\) has binary maximal heterogeneity at radius \(\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}}\) when \(\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}}\ge0\), every cell satisfies \(\left|\mu_{1k}^{\mathrm{bin}}(P)-\mu_{0k}^{\mathrm{bin}}(P)-\tau(P)\right|\le\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}}\), and some cell attains equality.  Suppose the published binary collision guarantee holds at overlap \(\epsilon\): there are constants \(C_\epsilon,b_\epsilon>0\) such that, for every \(n,d\in\mathbb N\) with \(d>0\), every binary law \(P\) with overlap \(\epsilon\), and every \(\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}}\in\mathbb R\) satisfying binary maximal heterogeneity at radius \(\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}}\),
\[
\left|
E_{P_n}[s]-\tau(P)
\right|
\le
\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}}
+
2\exp\left\{-b_\epsilon\frac{n^2}{\max\{n,d\}}\right\}
\]
and
\[
\operatorname{Var}_{P_n}(s)
\le
C_\epsilon\left(\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}}^2+\frac{d}{n^2}+\frac1n\right).
\]

Define
\[
u_{n,d}:=\frac{d^2}{n^2\log^2(en)}
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
h_{n,d,\sigma}:=\sigma^2+\frac{d}{n^2}.
\]
Then the published binary collision guarantee above and the following algebraic comparison hold simultaneously:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Pointwise comparison.)} For every \(n,d\in\mathbb N\) and \(\sigma\in\mathbb R\) such that \(n>0\), \(d>0\), and \(0\le \sigma\le 2\),
\[
\min\{1,\min\{u_{n,d},h_{n,d,\sigma}\}\}\le h_{n,d,\sigma}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Asymptotic comparison.)} For every pair of sequences \(d_n\in\mathbb N\) and \(\sigma_n\in\mathbb R\) satisfying \(d_n>0\) and \(0\le\sigma_n\le2\) for all \(n>0\), if
\[
\frac{u_{n,d_n}}{h_{n,d_n,\sigma_n}}\to0
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\frac{d_n}{n\log(en)}\to0,
\]
then
\[
\frac{\min\{1,\min\{u_{n,d_n},h_{n,d_n,\sigma_n}\}\}}
{h_{n,d_n,\sigma_n}}
\to0 .
\]
\end{itemize}

blocks.title: Binary exact-homogeneity source target
blocks.body: For a binary-outcome fixed-sample law \(P\) in the uniform-mass exact-homogeneity source family, let \(\mu_{ak}\) denote the conditional response mean in arm \(a\in\{0,1\}\) and cell \(k\in\{1,\ldots,d\}\). The source target is\[\psi(P):=\frac{1}{d}\sum_{k=1}^{d}(\mu_{1k}-\mu_{0k}).\]

blocks.title: Fixed-sample binary homogeneous experiment
blocks.body:
For integers \(n,d\ge1\) and \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), let \(\mathcal H_{n,d}^{\mathrm{bin}}(\epsilon)\) be the fixed-sample binary-outcome exactly homogeneous source experiment consisting of the product laws \(P^{\otimes n}\) generated by laws \(P\in\mathcal H_d^{\mathrm{bin}}(\epsilon)\). Its binary average response contrast is
\[
\psi(P)=\frac1d\sum_{k=1}^d\{\mu_{1k}^{\mathrm{bin}}(P)-\mu_{0k}^{\mathrm{bin}}(P)\}.
\]

blocks.title: Binary collision lower bound
Same-cell cross moment
Distinct-cell cross moment
Shifted coefficient envelope
blocks.body:
Let \(K\) be a positive integer, let \(B,p\in\mathbb R\), and define, for \(0\le j\le K-2\),
\[
g_{Kj}
:=
(-1)^j
\frac{2^{2j+3}}{K(K+j+2)}
\binom{K+j+2}{2j+4}.
\]
Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Positive scale.)} \(B>0\).
\item \textbf{(Nonnegative mass.)} \(p\ge 0\).
\item \textbf{(Budget bound.)} \(p\le B\).
\end{itemize}
Then
\[
\sum_{j=0}^{K-2}
\left|\frac{g_{Kj}}{B^{j+1}}\right|p^{j+2}
\le
B\,6^K.
\]

blocks.title: Empirical arm-cell mean \(\widehat\mu_{ak}\)
blocks.body: For a block of observations \(O_i=(X_i,A_i,Y_i)\), define the arm-cell count and outcome total by \[N_{ak}:=\sum_i \mathbf 1\{X_i=k,A_i=a\},\qquad S_{ak}:=\sum_i \mathbf 1\{X_i=k,A_i=a\}Y_i .\] The empirical arm-cell mean is \[\widehat\mu_{ak}:=\begin{cases}S_{ak}/N_{ak},&N_{ak}>0,\\ 0,&N_{ak}=0.\end{cases}\]

blocks.title: Fixed branch risk bound
blocks.body:
For every overlap parameter \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), there is a constant \(C_{\epsilon}>0\) such that the following holds.  Let \(d,m,K\in\mathbb N\), let \(M,\sigma,B,\beta\in\mathbb R\), let \(P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}\) as in \cref{obj:def:model-class}, and let \(H\subseteq\{1,\ldots,d\}\) be deterministic.  For one block of observations \(O_i=(X_i,A_i,Y_i)\), \(i=1,\ldots,m\), with joint law \(Q_P^{(m)}\), define
\[
\widehat R_H
:=
\sum_{k\in H}
\widehat p_k
\left\{
\widehat\mu_{1k}-\widehat\mu_{0k}
\right\},
\qquad
R_H(P)
:=
\sum_{k\in H}p_k\tau_k,
\]
where \(\widehat p_k\) is the empirical mass of cell \(k\) on the block and \(\widehat\mu_{ak}\) is the arm-cell sample mean on positive arm-cell counts, with the corresponding empty-cell contribution set to zero.  Let \(\widehat P_k\) be the light factorial-polynomial contribution at scale \(B\) and degree \(K\) from \cref{obj:def:polynomial-handle}, and define
\[
\Delta_H
:=
\frac{\widehat R_H-R_H(P)}{M}
+
\left\{
\sum_{k\in H^{\mathrm c}}\widehat P_k
-\frac{1}{M}\sum_{k\in H^{\mathrm c}}p_k\tau_k
\right\}.
\]
Let \(\mathcal E_{m,\epsilon,\beta}(H)\) denote the boundary-safe lower-mass missing envelope,
\[
\mathcal E_{m,\epsilon,\beta}(H)
=
\begin{cases}
\dfrac{|H|}{\{(m-2)\epsilon/2\}^2\beta},
& \{(m-2)\epsilon/2\}^2\beta>0,\\[1.2ex]
\sum_{k\in H}p_k,
& \{(m-2)\epsilon/2\}^2\beta\le 0.
\end{cases}
\]
Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Degree.)} \(2\le K\).
\item \textbf{(Scales.)} \(B>0\) and \(\beta>0\).
\item \textbf{(Heavy band.)} \(\beta\le p_k\) for every \(k\in H\).
\item \textbf{(Light scale.)} \(p_k\le B/4\) for every \(k\in H^{\mathrm c}\).
\item \textbf{(Block size.)} \(4(K+2)^2\le m\).
\item \textbf{(Shift calibration.)} \(4(K+2)/m\le 3B/4\).
\end{itemize}
Then
\[
\mathbb E_{Q_P^{(m)}}\!\left[\Delta_H^2\right]
\le
8\left\{
\frac{8\sum_{k\in H}p_k}{(m\vee 1)\epsilon}
+\frac{6}{m\vee 1}
+4\,\mathcal E_{m,\epsilon,\beta}(H)^2
\right\}
+
2\left\{
\frac{C_{\epsilon}}{m}
+C_{\epsilon}6^{2K}
\left(dB^2+\frac{d^2K^2B^2}{m}\right)
+\left(\frac{|H^{\mathrm c}|B}{\epsilon K^2}\right)^2
\right\}.
\]

blocks.title: Capped radial transport scale
blocks.body:
Let \(n,d\) be integers and let \(a,b,M,\sigma\in\mathbb R\).  Suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Sample size.)} \(n\ge 3\).
\item \textbf{(Alphabet size.)} \(d\ge 1\).
\item \textbf{(Scale.)} \(a\ge 0\).
\item \textbf{(Radial cap.)} \(0<b\le 4\).
\item \textbf{(Range.)} \(1\le (b/2)n\log(en)\).
\end{itemize}
Define the capped radial alphabet size from \cref{obj:def:least-favorable-handle} by
\[
d_{\mathrm{rad}}
:=
\min\left\{
d,\,
\max\left\{1,\left\lfloor (b/2)n\log(en)\right\rfloor\right\}
\right\}.
\]
Then
\[
\frac{ab^2}{128}M^2\sigma^2
\min\left\{1,\frac{d^2}{n^2\log^2(en)}\right\}
\le
\left(\frac{M\sigma}{2}\right)^2
\frac a2
\left\{
\frac1n+
\frac{d_{\mathrm{rad}}^2}{n^2\log^2 n}
\right\}.
\]

blocks.title: Capped exact transport scale
blocks.body:
For every overlap level \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), there exist constants
\(b_{\epsilon}^{\mathrm{ex}},c_{\epsilon}^{\mathrm{ex}}>0\) and a cutoff
\(N_{\epsilon}^{\mathrm{ex}}\in\mathbb N\) such that the following properties hold.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Capped alphabet.)} For every pair of integers \(n,d\ge1\), define the exact capped alphabet size from \cref{obj:def:least-favorable-handle} by
\[
d_{\mathrm{ex}}
=
\min\left\{d,\max\left\{1,\left\lfloor b_{\epsilon}^{\mathrm{ex}}n^2\right\rfloor\right\}\right\}.
\]
Then \(0<d_{\mathrm{ex}}\le d\), and whenever \(N_{\epsilon}^{\mathrm{ex}}\le n\),
\[
d_{\mathrm{ex}}\le b_{\epsilon}^{\mathrm{ex}}n^2 .
\]

\item \textbf{(Estimator-wise source risk.)} For every \(n,d\ge1\), with \(d_{\mathrm{ex}}\) defined above, there is a real number \(L_{\mathrm{ex}}=L_{\mathrm{ex}}(n,d)\) such that every measurable estimator
\[
\widehat\psi:\bigl(\{1,\ldots,n\}\to \bigl(\{1,\ldots,d_{\mathrm{ex}}\}\times\{0,1\}\times\{0,1\}\bigr)\bigr)\to\mathbb R
\]
admits an exactly homogeneous binary law \(R\) over \(d_{\mathrm{ex}}\) cells at overlap \(\epsilon\) for which
\[
L_{\mathrm{ex}}
\le
\mathbb E_{Q_R^{(n)}}\!\left[
\{\widehat\psi-\psi(R)\}^2
\right].
\]

\item \textbf{(Transport normalization.)} For every \(n,d\ge1\), with the same \(L_{\mathrm{ex}}(n,d)\), and for every \(M\in\mathbb R\),
\[
c_{\epsilon}^{\mathrm{ex}}M^2
\left\{\frac1n+\min\left(1,\frac d{n^2}\right)\right\}
\le
M^2L_{\mathrm{ex}} .
\]
\end{itemize}

blocks.title: Finite-sample radial scale
blocks.body:
Let \(n,d,N\in\mathbb N\) satisfy \(1\le n\le N\), and let \(M,\sigma\in\mathbb R\).  Define
\[
u_{n,d}=\frac{d^2}{n^2\log^2(en)}.
\]
Then
\[
\frac{1}{800N}\,M^2\sigma^2\min\{1,u_{n,d}\}
\le
\left(\frac{M\sigma}{2}\right)^2\frac{1}{200n}.
\]

blocks.title: Exact binary lower bound
blocks.body:
Fix \(0<\epsilon<1/2\).  For integers \(n,d\) with \(d>0\), let \(\mathcal H_{n,d}^{\mathrm{bin}}(\epsilon)\) be the fixed-sample binary-outcome experiment with cell masses \(p_k=1/d\), overlap \(\epsilon\le \pi_k\le 1-\epsilon\), conditional response means in \([0,1]\), and a common cell treatment effect, and write
\[
\psi(P)=\frac{1}{d}\sum_{k=1}^d(\mu_{1k}-\mu_{0k}).
\]
There exist constants \(a_\epsilon,b_\epsilon>0\) and an integer \(N_\epsilon\) such that, for every \(n,d\in\mathbb N\) with \(d>0\), \(N_\epsilon\le n\), and \(d\le b_\epsilon n^2\),
\[
a_\epsilon\left(\frac{1}{n}+\frac{d}{n^2}\right)
\le
\inf_{\widehat\psi}\sup_{P^{\otimes n}\in\mathcal H_{n,d}^{\mathrm{bin}}(\epsilon)}
E_P\!\left[(\widehat\psi-\psi(P))^2\right].
\]

blocks.title: Factorial covariance bound
Binary source law classes
blocks.body:
For an overlap parameter \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), let \(\mathcal D_d^{\mathrm{bin}}(\epsilon)\) be the class of binary \(d\)-cell full-data laws for \((X,A,B(0),B(1),B)\), with \(X\in\{1,\ldots,d\}\), \(A,B(0),B(1),B\in\{0,1\}\), consistency \(B=B(A)\), conditional exchangeability \((B(0),B(1))\perp A\mid X\), arbitrary cell masses \(p_k\), propensities \(\pi_k\) satisfying \(\epsilon\le\pi_k\le1-\epsilon\) on every positive-mass cell, and arm means \(\mu_{ak}^{\mathrm{bin}}=E[B\mid A=a,X=k]\in[0,1]\). Define its uniform-mass exactly homogeneous subclass by
\[
\mathcal H_d^{\mathrm{bin}}(\epsilon)
:=
\left\{
P\in\mathcal D_d^{\mathrm{bin}}(\epsilon):
p_k(P)=\frac1d\ \text{for every }k,\ 
\mu_{1k}^{\mathrm{bin}}(P)-\mu_{0k}^{\mathrm{bin}}(P)
=
\mu_{1\ell}^{\mathrm{bin}}(P)-\mu_{0\ell}^{\mathrm{bin}}(P)
\ \text{for all }k,\ell
\right\}.
\]

blocks.title: Affine binary-to-real embedding
blocks.body:
For \(M\ge1\), define \(\Phi_M\) as the affine pushforward that sends a binary \(d\)-cell law \(P\) to the real-outcome \(d\)-cell law obtained from
\[
Y(a):=M\{B(a)-1/2\},
\qquad
Y=Y(A).
\]
Under \(\Phi_M\), the cell masses and propensities agree with those of \(P\), each positive arm-cell conditional outcome law is pushed forward by \(b\mapsto M(b-1/2)\), and
\[
\mu_{ak}(\Phi_M(P))=M\{\mu_{ak}^{\mathrm{bin}}(P)-1/2\},
\qquad
\tau_k(\Phi_M(P))=M\{\mu_{1k}^{\mathrm{bin}}(P)-\mu_{0k}^{\mathrm{bin}}(P)\}.
\]

blocks.title: Mean-squared error \(\operatorname{MSE}_{P^{\prime}}(T)\)
blocks.body: For a real-outcome law \(P^{\prime}\) and a total estimator \(T\) of the \(n\)-sample, define its mean-squared error at \(P^{\prime}\) by \[\operatorname{MSE}_{P^{\prime}}(T):=E_{Q_{P^{\prime}}^{(n)}}\left[\left(T-\tau(P^{\prime})\right)^2\right],\] where \(Q_{P^{\prime}}^{(n)}=(P_O^{\prime})^{\otimes n}\) is the observed product law and \(\tau(P^{\prime})\) is the average treatment effect functional.

blocks.title: Affine subclass transfer
blocks.body:
Let \(\mathcal D_d^{\mathrm{bin}}(\epsilon)\) and \(\mathcal H_d^{\mathrm{bin}}(\epsilon)\) be the binary source classes of \cref{obj:synth_2}, whose defining conditions are recalled here only through the overlap and homogeneity constraints that this proposition uses:
\[
\mathcal D_d^{\mathrm{bin}}(\epsilon)
:=
\{P:\text{ for every positive-mass cell }k,\ 
\epsilon\le \pi_k(P)\le 1-\epsilon\}.
\]
and, for the uniform-mass exactly homogeneous subclass,
\[
\mathcal H_d^{\mathrm{bin}}(\epsilon)
:=
\left\{
P\in\mathcal D_d^{\mathrm{bin}}(\epsilon):
p_k(P)=\frac1d\ \text{for every }k,\ 
\mu_{1k}^{\mathrm{bin}}(P)-\mu_{0k}^{\mathrm{bin}}(P)
=
\mu_{1\ell}^{\mathrm{bin}}(P)-\mu_{0\ell}^{\mathrm{bin}}(P)
\ \text{for all }k,\ell
\right\}.
\]
For every overlap parameter \(\epsilon\) with \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), there are constants
\(c_{\mathrm{ex}},c_{\mathrm{rad}},b_{\mathrm{rad}},C_{\mathrm{up}}>0\) and a polynomial
calibration handle, consisting of a cutoff \(K_0\in\mathbb N\) and an active-range multiplier
\(A>0\) such that
\[
K_0\le n,\qquad d\le A n\log(en)
\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad
2\le K_n
\]
for all \(n,d\ge1\), where \(K_n\) is the polynomial degree of \cref{obj:def:polynomial-handle}, with the following property.  For every \(d\ge1\) and \(M\ge1\), there is an affine embedding map \(\Phi_M\), sending each binary \(d\)-cell law to a real-outcome \(d\)-cell law,
\[
\Phi_M:\{d\text{-cell binary laws}\}\longrightarrow \{d\text{-cell real-outcome laws}\},
\]
with the following properties:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Affine embedding.)} For every binary law \(P\), \(\Phi_M(P)\) is the affine pushforward \(B(a)\mapsto M\{B(a)-1/2\}\): its observed law is the pushforward of the binary observed law, its cell masses and propensities agree with those of \(P\), each positive arm-cell conditional outcome law is pushed forward by \(b\mapsto M(b-1/2)\), each arm-cell mean is \(M\) times the corresponding binary mean minus \(M/2\), and its full-data law is induced by an affine pushforward of a binary full-data coupling.

\item \textbf{(Unrestricted inclusion.)} If \(P\in\mathcal D_d^{\mathrm{bin}}(\epsilon)\), then \(\Phi_M(P)\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}^{\mathrm{unr}}\), the class in \cref{obj:def:unrestricted-class}.

\item \textbf{(Exact homogeneous inclusion.)} If \(P\in\mathcal H_d^{\mathrm{bin}}(\epsilon)\), then
\[
\Phi_M(P)\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,0},
\]
with \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}\) as in \cref{obj:def:model-class}.

\item \textbf{(Strict image.)} For every \(0\le\sigma\le2\), there exists a real-outcome law \(Q\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}\) that is the image of no binary law:
\[
\Phi_M(P)\ne Q
\]
for every binary law \(P\).

\item \textbf{(Lower transfers and upper estimator.)} Write \(\operatorname{MSE}_{P^{\prime}}(T):=E_{Q_{P^{\prime}}^{(n)}}\left[\left(T-\tau(P^{\prime})\right)^2\right]\) for the mean-squared error of a total estimator \(T\) under the \(n\)-sample law of a real-outcome law \(P^{\prime}\). For every \(n\ge1\) and \(0\le\sigma\le2\), if \(d\le c_{\mathrm{ex}}n^2\), then every total measurable estimator with values in \([-M,M]\) has some \(P\in\mathcal H_d^{\mathrm{bin}}(\epsilon)\) satisfying
\[
c_{\mathrm{ex}}M^2\left(\frac1n+\frac{d}{n^2}\right)
\le
\operatorname{MSE}_{\Phi_M(P)}(\widehat\tau),
\]
and the minimax risk in \cref{obj:def:minimax-risk} satisfies
\[
c_{\mathrm{ex}}M^2\left(\frac1n+\frac{d}{n^2}\right)
\le
\mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}.
\]
For all \(n\ge1\) and \(0\le\sigma\le2\), the radius-channel transfer gives
\[
c_{\mathrm{rad}}M^2\sigma^2\min\{1,u_{n,d}\}
\le
\mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\sigma},
\]
together with a transfer certificate with constants \(c_{\mathrm{rad}}\) and \(b_{\mathrm{rad}}\).  The estimator \(T_n^{\mathrm{poly}}\) determined by the polynomial calibration handle is measurable, takes values in \([-M,M]\), and for every \(Q\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}\),
\[
\operatorname{MSE}_{Q}(T_n^{\mathrm{poly}})
\le
C_{\mathrm{up}}M^2\left(\frac1n+\min\{1,u_{n,d}\}\right).
\]
\end{itemize}

blocks.title: All-alphabet polynomial upper bound
blocks.body:
For every overlap parameter \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), there exist a constant \(C_{\epsilon}>0\) and a polynomial handle, consisting of a cutoff \(N_{\epsilon}\in\mathbb N\) and an active-range multiplier \(\rho_{\epsilon}>0\) such that
\[
N_{\epsilon}\le n,\qquad d\le \rho_{\epsilon}n\log(en)
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
2\le K_n
\]
for all integers \(n,d\ge1\), with the following properties.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Complexity.)} The handle admits a constant \(C_{\mathrm{op}}\in\mathbb N\), independent of \(n,d\), and \(M\), such that for every \(n,d\) and \(M\) the post-aggregation polynomial program for \(T_n^{\mathrm{poly}}\) has at most
\[
C_{\mathrm{op}}(d+1)(K_n+1)^2
\]
arithmetic operations.
\item \textbf{(Total bounded estimator.)} For every pair of integers \(n,d\ge1\) and every \(M\ge1\), the estimator \(T_n^{\mathrm{poly}}\) determined by this handle is a measurable function of the \(n\)-sample observed data and satisfies
\[
T_n^{\mathrm{poly}}(s)\in[-M,M]
\]
for every sample \(s\).
\item \textbf{(Risk bound.)} For every pair of integers \(n,d\ge1\), every \(M\ge1\), every \(0\le\sigma\le2\), and every \(P\in\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}\) as in \cref{obj:def:model-class},
\[
\mathbb E_{Q_P^{(n)}}\!\left[\{T_n^{\mathrm{poly}}-\tau(P)\}^2\right]
\le
C_{\epsilon}M^2
\left\{
\frac{1}{n}
+
\min\!\left(1,\frac{d^2}{n^2\log^2(en)}\right)
\right\}.
\]
\end{itemize}

blocks.title: All-d radius converse
blocks.body:
For every \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), there exist constants \(c_{\epsilon}\) and \(b_{\epsilon}^{\mathrm{rad}}\) such that
\[
0<c_{\epsilon}\le 1,
\qquad
0<b_{\epsilon}^{\mathrm{rad}}.
\]
For all integers \(n,d\ge 1\), all \(M\ge 1\), and all \(0\le \sigma\le 2\), the minimax mean-squared risk \(\mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}\) of \cref{obj:def:minimax-risk} satisfies
\[
c_{\epsilon}M^2
\left\{
\frac1n+\min\left(1,\frac d{n^2}\right)
+\sigma^2\min\left(1,\frac{d^2}{n^2\log^2(en)}\right)
\right\}
\le
\mathsf R_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}.
\]
Moreover, for the same constants and every such \(n,d,M,\sigma\), there are a capped alphabet size \(d_{\mathrm{rad}}\), a source family, a padding map into \(\{1,\ldots,d\}\), an embedding into \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}\), and a coupling realizing the radius-channel construction with source constant \(b_{\epsilon}^{\mathrm{rad}}\). Along this realization, for all source laws \(P_0,P_1\),
\[
\tau(P_1)-\tau(P_0)
=
M\frac{\sigma}{2}
\{\psi(P_1)-\psi(P_0)\},
\]
and for every estimator \(\widehat\tau\) taking values in \([-M,M]\), some source law \(P\) satisfies
\[
c_{\epsilon}M^2\sigma^2
\min\left(1,\frac{d^2}{n^2\log^2(en)}\right)
\le
\mathbb E_P\{(\widehat\tau-\tau(P))^2\}.
\]
